content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: Actions
description: What an action is, how it takes a clip to an end state over a span of time, and how numbers, colours and switches change along the way.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An action makes a clip change over time: a zoom into a screen recording, a fade of the volume, a title that slides and changes colour. You say where the clip ends up, and the action's span and curve say how it gets there.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'The action lane on each clip in the timeline']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.window"
  alt="The editor with a lower third selected. On the timeline the graphic clip holds a numbered action band, the Clip tab's action lane reads 1, editing 1, and the inspector shows the values the clip reaches at the action's end."
/>

## What an action is

An action is a span of time on one clip. Over that span, the clip's properties move from whatever they were when the span began to the action's **end state**, along the action's curve.

Actions take the place of keyframes. You don't set a value at each moment. You set what the clip ends at, and the span and the curve do the rest.

Actions on one clip can't overlap, and you can't make one that runs past the clip's end. A later trim can leave an action running past the end, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).

To make one, see [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), then [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## The end state is held

When the span is over, the clip keeps the end state until a later action changes it. An action that takes the scale to 200% leaves the clip at 200% for the rest of its length. The clip doesn't drift back on its own.

To go back, add a second action whose end state names the old value. [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) does this for a zoom.

## Clip time

An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. An action that starts at 2 seconds starts 2 seconds into the clip, wherever the clip sits. Move the clip and its actions go with it.

The **Start** field in the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows this time.

## Several actions on a clip

A clip can have as many actions as fit end to end. They run in time order, and each one starts from the state the earlier ones left behind.

An action only changes what its end state names. If action 1 takes the scale to 200% and action 2 names only the opacity, the scale stays at 200% through action 2 while the opacity moves.

## Action numbers

Actions are numbered in time order, and an action has the same number on the timeline and in the Clip tab. The number is a position, not a name, so adding an action before an existing one moves the later ones up by one.

## Easing curves

A curve sets how a value moves across the span. The same four curves serve actions, zooms, speed ramps and transitions.

| Curve | In the action lane | How it moves | Halfway through the span, the value is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear | Linear | At a constant speed | 50% of the way there |
| Ease In | In | Starts slowly, ends fast | 25% of the way there |
| Ease Out | Out | Starts fast, ends slowly | 75% of the way there |
| Ease In Out | In Out | Slow at both ends | 50% of the way there |

The action lane's **Curve** pop-up shows the short names, with a small drawing of the curve beside it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/). A transition's **Curve** pop-up shows the full names. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).

### Default curves

A new action from **Add Action** is **Linear**. A zoom action, from Zoom to Region or Zoom Back, is **Ease In Out**.

## How values change over an action

What happens to a property depends on what kind of value it is. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) goes through them section by section.

### Numbers

Numbers ramp along the action's curve. That covers position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, volume, a filter's amount, a grade's sliders and a graphic's number properties.

An agent can aim a number past what the property can hold. Frame Job keeps the value in the action as written and brings it into range as the clip is drawn, so an opacity aimed at 200% reaches 100% before the action ends and stays there.

### Colours

Colours ramp too, through OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. See [Colours blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab).

### Switches, popups and text

An on/off box, a filter's kind, a font and a graphic's string, boolean or image property have nothing in between. They hold their value for the whole span, then switch to the end value when the action ends. Their rows are tagged "at end" in the Clip tab.

The same goes for a section you turn on inside an action, such as a shadow or an outline. Its numbers have nothing to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends.

:::tip
To fade a shadow in, turn it on for the clip with **Opacity** at 0%, then add an action that raises **Opacity**. The opacity ramps, because both ends of it exist.
:::

### Lists

Filters and obscure regions are lists, and they ramp entry by entry while both ends have the same number of entries.

| If | Then |
| --- | --- |
| Both ends have the same number of entries | Each entry's numbers ramp to the entry in the same place at the other end |
| One entry changes kind, or a region changes shape | Only that entry switches at the end, and the others still ramp |
| The list's length changes | The whole list switches at the end |

### Colour curves

Curves in the **Color** sub-tab always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point, and a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points. Two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action.

## Related

- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
- [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/)

---
title: Add an action
description: Add a 1-second action at the playhead, see when Add Action is available, and find out why Frame Job might not place one.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Add Action puts a new [action](/motion/actions/) on the selected clip at the playhead, ready for you to say what it animates to.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ + (Add Action)"
  tools="add_action"
/>

## Add Action

<Steps>

1. Select a clip and put the playhead over it.

2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Add Action** and the **+** button in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) do the same.

</Steps>

The new action starts at the playhead, lasts 1 second and uses the **Linear** curve. It's one undo step.

## A new action starts empty

A new action's end state is empty, so it changes nothing until you edit it. The band appears, and the clip looks and sounds the same as before.

The action is selected as it's added, so the Clip tab is ready for its end state. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/). The playhead stays where it is.

## When Add Action is available

Add Action needs the playhead over a selected clip. Otherwise **Clip ▸ Add Action** is greyed out, and the action lane's **+** button beeps.

## Several clips selected

With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and isn't selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select that clip alone to edit the new action.

## When an action is refused

The new action needs a clear second after the playhead. Frame Job beeps and adds nothing when the action would:

- overlap another action on the clip, or
- run past the clip's end.

The reason appears at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:".

Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first, or [shorten an existing action](/motion/change-an-action/). A clip shorter than 1 second has no room for an action from Add Action.

## Other commands that make actions

These commands write ordinary actions. They show as bands and edit like any other.

| Command | What it adds |
| --- | --- |
| [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action that zooms to a rectangle you draw |
| [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action back to the clip's own size and place |
| [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | One action for Ramp Up and Ramp Down, two for Speed Dip and Speed Burst |
| [Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…](/recording/auto-zoom/) | Zoom actions planned from a recording's cursor file |
| [Clip ▸ Follow Subject…](/framing/follow-subject/) | Moves that keep a subject in frame |
| [Clip ▸ Camera Layout](/framing/camera-layouts/) | Moves from one layout to the next |
| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | An action for each point you add with <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click |

Only Add Action, Zoom to Region and Zoom Back select the action they make.

## With an agent

`add_action` takes its own length, so an agent can place an action shorter than 1 second where Add Action has no room. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)

2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Add Action** and the **+** button in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) do the same.

</Steps>

The new action starts at the playhead, lasts 1 second and uses the **Linear** curve. It's one undo step.

## A new action starts empty

A new action's end state is empty, so it changes nothing until you edit it. The band appears, and the clip looks and sounds the same as before.

The action is selected as it's added, so the Clip tab is ready for its end state. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/). The playhead stays where it is.

## When Add Action is available

Add Action needs the playhead over a selected clip. Otherwise **Clip ▸ Add Action** is greyed out, and the action lane's **+** button beeps.

## Several clips selected

With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and isn't selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select that clip alone to edit the new action.

## When an action is refused

The new action needs a clear second after the playhead. Frame Job beeps and adds nothing when the action would:

- overlap another action on the clip, or
- run past the clip's end.

The reason appears at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:".

Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first, or [shorten an existing action](/motion/change-an-action/). A clip shorter than 1 second has no room for an action from Add Action.

These commands write ordinary actions. They show as bands and edit like any other.

| Command | What it adds |
| --- | --- |
| [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action that zooms to a rectangle you draw |
| [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action back to the clip's own size and place |
| [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | One action for Ramp Up and Ramp Down, two for Speed Dip and Speed Burst |
| [Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…](/recording/auto-zoom/) | Zoom actions planned from a recording's cursor file |
| [Clip ▸ Follow Subject…](/framing/follow-subject/) | Moves that keep a subject in frame |
| [Clip ▸ Camera Layout](/framing/camera-layouts/) | Moves from one layout to the next |
| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | An action for each point you add with <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click |

Only Add Action, Zoom to Region and Zoom Back select the action they make.

## With an agent

`add_action` takes its own length, so an agent can place an action shorter than 1 second where Add Action has no room. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

---
title: Select an action
description: Select an action from its band or by moving the playhead into it, see which one is selected, and leave it to edit the clip again.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Selecting an action points the Clip tab at that action's end state. While one is selected, the fields show and set what the clip reaches at the action's end, not the clip's own values.

<AtAGlance
  keys="Esc"
  where={['A band on the timeline', 'Clip tab ▸ action lane']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with an action selected. The action lane reads ACTIONS 1, editing 1, with a solid numbered band from about a fifth to two thirds of the clip and the playhead line across it. Below it are a start time of 00:00:01:00, a length of 2.00 s and the curve Linear. The Graphic sub-tab and the Properties section each show a diamond and 3, and the rows accent, size and boxed carry a diamond, with boxed tagged at end."
/>

## Click a band

Click an action's band on the timeline or in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). The action is selected, and the Clip tab then edits its end values.

The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. When the action ends with the clip, the playhead stops one frame short, because the clip's very end has no picture.

Clicking a band on a clip that's part of a multi-clip selection selects just that clip and its action.

On the timeline the action is selected when you press. In the Clip tab's lane it's selected when you let go, so a drag in the lane selects the band when you drop it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

## Adding selects the action

An action made with [Add Action](/motion/add-an-action/), [Zoom to Region or Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) is selected as it's added. The playhead doesn't move for this.

## Play or scrub into a span

While a clip is the only one selected, moving the playhead into one of its actions selects that action. Playing, scrubbing and stepping all count.

Selecting a clip counts too. If the playhead is already inside one of its actions, that action is selected along with the clip.

It takes an entry into the span. An edit that puts a span under a still playhead selects nothing, and neither does an undo or a redo.

## How a selected action looks

On the timeline:

- The action's band is solid.
- A wash runs down the clip under the action's span.
- The span is shaded on the ruler.

In the Clip tab:

- The action lane is tinted, and its header adds "· editing N" after the count.
- The band is solid, and the **Clip** chip is no longer highlighted.
- A detail row appears with the action's start, length, curve and trash button.

## The Clip chip

The **Clip** chip sits at the start of the action lane. It's highlighted while no action is selected, which tells you the fields edit the clip. Click it while an action is selected to leave the action.

## Leave an action

Do any of these, and the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again:

- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>.
- Click the **Clip** chip.
- Select a different clip.

Moving the playhead out of the span doesn't leave the action. It stays selected, and the fields keep editing its end state.

After <kbd>Esc</kbd> or the **Clip** chip, the playhead can stay inside the span without selecting the action again. It's selected the next time the playhead leaves and comes back.

With no action selected, <kbd>Esc</kbd> does whatever it would do otherwise.

## Selection is not an edit

Selecting an action isn't an undo step, and it isn't saved with the project. A project always opens with no action selected.

## Good to know

- Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select a second clip and the action is deselected. The action lane then reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
- Where two bands sit under the pointer, the one painted on top wins, which is the later one.
- Clicking a band that touches the next action puts the playhead on the first frame of that next action, but the one you clicked stays selected.
- Removing the selected action deselects it.

## Related

- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Actions](/motion/actions/)

---
title: Actions
description: What an action is, how it takes a clip to an end state over a span of time, and how numbers, colours and switches change along the way.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An action makes a clip change over time: a zoom into a screen recording, a fade of the volume, a title that slides and changes colour. You say where the clip ends up, and the action's span and curve say how it gets there.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'The action lane on each clip in the timeline']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.window"
  alt="The editor with a lower third selected. On the timeline the graphic clip holds a numbered action band, the Clip tab's action lane reads 1, editing 1, and the inspector shows the values the clip reaches at the action's end."
/>

## What an action is

An action is a span of time on one clip. Over that span, the clip's properties move from whatever they were when the span began to the action's **end state**, along the action's curve.

Actions take the place of keyframes. You don't set a value at each moment. You set what the clip ends at, and the span and the curve do the rest.

Actions on one clip can't overlap, and you can't make one that runs past the clip's end. A later trim can leave an action running past the end, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).

To make one, see [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), then [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

## The end state is held

When the span is over, the clip keeps the end state until a later action changes it. An action that takes the scale to 200% leaves the clip at 200% for the rest of its length. The clip doesn't drift back on its own.

To go back, add a second action whose end state names the old value. [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) does this for a zoom.

## Clip time

An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. An action that starts at 2 seconds starts 2 seconds into the clip, wherever the clip sits. Move the clip and its actions go with it.

The **Start** field in the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows this time.

## Several actions on a clip

A clip can have as many actions as fit end to end. They run in time order, and each one starts from the state the earlier ones left behind.

An action only changes what its end state names. If action 1 takes the scale to 200% and action 2 names only the opacity, the scale stays at 200% through action 2 while the opacity moves.

## Action numbers

Actions are numbered in time order, and an action has the same number on the timeline and in the Clip tab. The number is a position, not a name, so adding an action before an existing one moves the later ones up by one.

## Easing curves

A curve sets how a value moves across the span. The same four curves serve actions, zooms, speed ramps and transitions.

| Curve | In the action lane | How it moves | Halfway through the span, the value is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear | Linear | At a constant speed | 50% of the way there |
| Ease In | In | Starts slowly, ends fast | 25% of the way there |
| Ease Out | Out | Starts fast, ends slowly | 75% of the way there |
| Ease In Out | In Out | Slow at both ends | 50% of the way there |

The action lane's **Curve** pop-up shows the short names, with a small drawing of the curve beside it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/). A transition's **Curve** pop-up shows the full names. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).

### Default curves

A new action from **Add Action** is **Linear**. A zoom action, from Zoom to Region or Zoom Back, is **Ease In Out**.

## How values change over an action

What happens to a property depends on what kind of value it is. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) goes through them section by section.

### Numbers

Numbers ramp along the action's curve. That covers position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, volume, a filter's amount, a grade's sliders and a graphic's number properties.

An agent can aim a number past what the property can hold. Frame Job keeps the value in the action as written and brings it into range as the clip is drawn, so an opacity aimed at 200% reaches 100% before the action ends and stays there.

### Colours

Colours ramp too, through OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. See [Colours blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab).

### Switches, popups and text

An on/off box, a filter's kind, a font and a graphic's string, boolean or image property have nothing in between. They hold their value for the whole span, then switch to the end value when the action ends. Their rows are tagged "at end" in the Clip tab.

The same goes for a section you turn on inside an action, such as a shadow or an outline. Its numbers have nothing to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends.

:::tip
To fade a shadow in, turn it on for the clip with **Opacity** at 0%, then add an action that raises **Opacity**. The opacity ramps, because both ends of it exist.
:::

### Lists

Filters and obscure regions are lists, and they ramp entry by entry while both ends have the same number of entries.

| If | Then |
| --- | --- |
| Both ends have the same number of entries | Each entry's numbers ramp to the entry in the same place at the other end |
| One entry changes kind, or a region changes shape | Only that entry switches at the end, and the others still ramp |
| The list's length changes | The whole list switches at the end |

### Colour curves

Curves in the **Color** sub-tab always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point, and a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points. Two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action.

## Related

- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
- [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/)

Below it are a start time of 00:00:01:00, a length of 2.00 s and the curve Linear. The Graphic sub-tab and the Properties section each show a diamond and 3, and the rows accent, size and boxed carry a diamond, with boxed tagged at end."
/>

## Click a band

Click an action's band on the timeline or in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). The action is selected, and the Clip tab then edits its end values.

The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. When the action ends with the clip, the playhead stops one frame short, because the clip's very end has no picture.

Clicking a band on a clip that's part of a multi-clip selection selects just that clip and its action.

On the timeline the action is selected when you press. In the Clip tab's lane it's selected when you let go, so a drag in the lane selects the band when you drop it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

## Adding selects the action

An action made with [Add Action](/motion/add-an-action/), [Zoom to Region or Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) is selected as it's added. The playhead doesn't move for this.

## Play or scrub into a span

While a clip is the only one selected, moving the playhead into one of its actions selects that action. Playing, scrubbing and stepping all count.

Selecting a clip counts too. If the playhead is already inside one of its actions, that action is selected along with the clip.

It takes an entry into the span. An edit that puts a span under a still playhead selects nothing, and neither does an undo or a redo.

## How a selected action looks

On the timeline:

- The action's band is solid.
- A wash runs down the clip under the action's span.
- The span is shaded on the ruler.

In the Clip tab:

- The action lane is tinted, and its header adds "· editing N" after the count.
- The band is solid, and the **Clip** chip is no longer highlighted.
- A detail row appears with the action's start, length, curve and trash button.

## The Clip chip

The **Clip** chip sits at the start of the action lane. It's highlighted while no action is selected, which tells you the fields edit the clip. Click it while an action is selected to leave the action.

## Leave an action

Do any of these, and the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again:

- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>.
- Click the **Clip** chip.
- Select a different clip.

Moving the playhead out of the span doesn't leave the action. It stays selected, and the fields keep editing its end state.

After <kbd>Esc</kbd> or the **Clip** chip, the playhead can stay inside the span without selecting the action again. It's selected the next time the playhead leaves and comes back.

With no action selected, <kbd>Esc</kbd> does whatever it would do otherwise.

## Selection is not an edit

Selecting an action isn't an undo step, and it isn't saved with the project. A project always opens with no action selected.

## Good to know

- Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select a second clip and the action is deselected. The action lane then reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
- Where two bands sit under the pointer, the one painted on top wins, which is the later one.
- Clicking a band that touches the next action puts the playhead on the first frame of that next action, but the one you clicked stays selected.
- Removing the selected action deselects it.

## Related

- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Actions](/motion/actions/)

---
title: What an action can animate
description: Which properties ramp across an action, which switch at its end, and which can't animate at all, sub-tab by sub-tab.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate most of what's in the Clip tab. This page goes through the tab by sub-tab, so you can see what ramps smoothly, what switches when the action ends, and what can't animate.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab, with an action selected"
  tools="set_action_end"
/>

With an action selected, the Clip tab marks each row. A row that switches shows "at end" once the action changes it, and a row that can't animate shows ⊘. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks.

One rule applies everywhere. A section you turn on inside an action has no numbers to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends. For a gradual start, turn the section on for the clip first and animate its numbers. Turning a section off inside an action turns it off when the action ends.

## Picture

An action can animate every value in the **Picture** sub-tab.

| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Transform](/canvas/transform/) | **Scale**, **Position X**, **Position Y**, **Rotation**, **Opacity**, [**Motion Blur**](/motion/motion-blur/) | **Blend** |
| [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) | | **Behind subject** |
| [Crop](/canvas/crop/) | **Left**, **Top**, **Right**, **Bottom** | |
| Corner Radius | **Radius** | |
| [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/) | **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness**, **Spill** | **Key out a color** |
| [Background](/effects/remove-background/) | **Edge**, **Feather** | **Background** |
| [Cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) | **Size**, **Ripple size** | **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks**, **Ripple color** |
| [Shadow](/effects/shadow/) | **Color**, **Opacity**, **Blur**, **Angle**, **Distance** | **Drop shadow** |
| [Filters](/effects/filters/) | Each filter's **Amount** | A filter's kind |
| [Reflection](/effects/reflection/) | **Opacity**, **Height**, **Gap**, **Falloff** | **Mirror the layer below itself** |
| [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) | **Center X**, **Center Y**, **Width**, **Height**, **Feather**, **Dim**, **Zoom** | **Spotlight a region**, **Shape** |
| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) | Each region's position, size, **Amount** and **Feather** | A region's kind and **Shape** |

Filters and obscure regions follow the [list rule](/motion/actions/#lists). Changing a value inside an existing entry animates, but adding or removing an entry [changes the clip](#what-never-animates).

## Color

An action can animate the whole grade in the **Color** sub-tab.

| Section | What animates |
| --- | --- |
| Light | Every slider |
| Color | Every slider |
| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Each wheel and its master strip |
| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Every channel, whatever the number of points |
| [Look](/color/looks/) | **Amount** |
| [Adjustment](/color/adjustment-clips/), on an adjustment clip | **Strength** |
| [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/), on an adjustment clip | Each range's numbers. **Invert** and turning a range on or off switch at the end |

Choosing a look or a LUT, changing it or removing it changes the clip itself, even with an action selected. Only **Amount** animates. If an agent gives an action a different look, it switches at the end. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Sound

An action can animate the **Sound** sub-tab's **Volume** and **Fades** sections, and every other audio setting apart from the few listed under [What never animates](#what-never-animates). A drag on the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) writes volume actions too.

Numbers ramp. Switches change when the action ends: **Mix to mono**, **Channels**, the EQ's slots and slopes, Hum's mains and harmonics, the Leveller's **Response**, and turning a section on or off. Voice Isolation's **Amount** ramps from 0 on a clip with none.

**Normalize** sets the clip's own level whatever is selected, and its row shows a small "clip" tag while an action is selected.

See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).

## Text

An action can animate the **Text** sub-tab's style, size and colours.

| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content | | The words |
| Font | **Size** | **Family**, **Style** |
| Style | **Color**, **Line spacing**, **Tracking** | **Align**, **Vertical**, **UPPERCASE** |
| Outline | **Width**, **Color** | **Outline** |
| Backdrop | **Fill**, **Padding**, **Radius** | **Backdrop** |
| Box | **Width** | **Mode** |
| Reveal | **In**, **Out** | **Reveal** |

Choosing one of the **Presets** with an action selected sets the action's end state, and each value then ramps or switches as above.

A word caption page's timing can't animate, because it belongs to the speech. There's no inspector section for its word colours and pop scale, so only an agent can put those in an action. They ramp when it does. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).

For the rows themselves, see [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).

## Graphics

An action can animate a graphic clip's properties in the **Properties** section of the **Graphic** sub-tab. Numbers and colours ramp, while strings, booleans, choices and images switch at the end. A property the graphic marks as not animatable shows ⊘, and so do the **Size** and **Timeline** sections.

See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

## Speed

An action can change a media clip's playback rate, which makes a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/). With an action selected, **Rate** in the **Clip** sub-tab's **Speed** section sets the rate the action ends at, and the clip holds that rate afterwards.

- The rate goes from ×0.1 to ×1000.
- The clip keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source.
- Frame Job won't set a rate that would read past the end of the media, and it names the largest rate that fits.
- Above ×12 the clip's sound is left out, and Frame Job asks first. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** always change the clip.

## What never animates

These rows change the clip itself whatever is selected. They're marked ⊘ in the Clip tab while an action is selected, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."

- **Clip sub-tab:** the [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Keep pitch** and **Fit to** in the Speed section.
- **Sound sub-tab:** Ducking, the fade shapes (**In shape** and **Out shape**), the Voice Effect, and a nest clip's **Mix to mono**.
- **Picture sub-tab:** the [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) section, **Remove background** and **Subject** in the Background section, and **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle** in the Cursor section.
- **Filters and Obscure:** adding or removing a filter or a region. Changing a value inside an existing entry still animates.
- **Shape sub-tab:** a [shape's](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) kind, stroke, fill, gradient and arrows. Its position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's, through the **Picture** sub-tab. Dragging a shape's handles on the canvas to resize it changes the shape itself.
- **Graphic sub-tab:** the **Size** and **Timeline** sections, and any property the graphic marks as not animatable.

A track's own volume, pan, compressor and limiter aren't part of a clip, so an action can't reach them.

## Colours blend in OKLab

Every colour an action animates blends through the OKLab colour space. It keeps the midpoints even and avoids the muddy middle of a straight RGB blend. Pure red to pure blue passes through `#8c53a2` halfway, for example, where a straight RGB blend would give a dark purple.

This covers the shadow, chroma key, text, outline, backdrop, word caption and graphic colours. Opacity moves separately from the colour. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact all the way through, and there's no setting for any of this.

Shape colours can't animate at all.

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)
- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)

- **Filters and Obscure:** adding or removing a filter or a region. Changing a value inside an existing entry still animates.
- **Shape sub-tab:** a [shape's](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) kind, stroke, fill, gradient and arrows. Its position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's, through the **Picture** sub-tab. Dragging a shape's handles on the canvas to resize it changes the shape itself.
- **Graphic sub-tab:** the **Size** and **Timeline** sections, and any property the graphic marks as not animatable.

A track's own volume, pan, compressor and limiter aren't part of a clip, so an action can't reach them.

## Colours blend in OKLab

Every colour an action animates blends through the OKLab colour space. It keeps the midpoints even and avoids the muddy middle of a straight RGB blend. Pure red to pure blue passes through `#8c53a2` halfway, for example, where a straight RGB blend would give a dark purple.

This covers the shadow, chroma key, text, outline, backdrop, word caption and graphic colours. Opacity moves separately from the colour. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact all the way through, and there's no setting for any of this.

Shape colours can't animate at all.

---
title: What an action can animate
description: Which properties ramp across an action, which switch at its end, and which can't animate at all, sub-tab by sub-tab.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate most of what's in the Clip tab. This page goes through the tab by sub-tab, so you can see what ramps smoothly, what switches when the action ends, and what can't animate.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab, with an action selected"
  tools="set_action_end"
/>

With an action selected, the Clip tab marks each row. A row that switches shows "at end" once the action changes it, and a row that can't animate shows ⊘. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks.

One rule applies everywhere. A section you turn on inside an action has no numbers to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends. For a gradual start, turn the section on for the clip first and animate its numbers. Turning a section off inside an action turns it off when the action ends.

## Picture

An action can animate every value in the **Picture** sub-tab.

| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Transform](/canvas/transform/) | **Scale**, **Position X**, **Position Y**, **Rotation**, **Opacity**, [**Motion Blur**](/motion/motion-blur/) | **Blend** |
| [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) | | **Behind subject** |
| [Crop](/canvas/crop/) | **Left**, **Top**, **Right**, **Bottom** | |
| Corner Radius | **Radius** | |
| [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/) | **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness**, **Spill** | **Key out a color** |
| [Background](/effects/remove-background/) | **Edge**, **Feather** | **Background** |
| [Cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) | **Size**, **Ripple size** | **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks**, **Ripple color** |
| [Shadow](/effects/shadow/) | **Color**, **Opacity**, **Blur**, **Angle**, **Distance** | **Drop shadow** |
| [Filters](/effects/filters/) | Each filter's **Amount** | A filter's kind |
| [Reflection](/effects/reflection/) | **Opacity**, **Height**, **Gap**, **Falloff** | **Mirror the layer below itself** |
| [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) | **Center X**, **Center Y**, **Width**, **Height**, **Feather**, **Dim**, **Zoom** | **Spotlight a region**, **Shape** |
| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) | Each region's position, size, **Amount** and **Feather** | A region's kind and **Shape** |

Filters and obscure regions follow the [list rule](/motion/actions/#lists). Changing a value inside an existing entry animates, but adding or removing an entry [changes the clip](#what-never-animates).

## Color

An action can animate the whole grade in the **Color** sub-tab.

| Section | What animates |
| --- | --- |
| Light | Every slider |
| Color | Every slider |
| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Each wheel and its master strip |
| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Every channel, whatever the number of points |
| [Look](/color/looks/) | **Amount** |
| [Adjustment](/color/adjustment-clips/), on an adjustment clip | **Strength** |
| [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/), on an adjustment clip | Each range's numbers. **Invert** and turning a range on or off switch at the end |

Choosing a look or a LUT, changing it or removing it changes the clip itself, even with an action selected. Only **Amount** animates. If an agent gives an action a different look, it switches at the end. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Sound

An action can animate the **Sound** sub-tab's **Volume** and **Fades** sections, and every other audio setting apart from the few listed under [What never animates](#what-never-animates). A drag on the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) writes volume actions too.

Numbers ramp. Switches change when the action ends: **Mix to mono**, **Channels**, the EQ's slots and slopes, Hum's mains and harmonics, the Leveller's **Response**, and turning a section on or off. Voice Isolation's **Amount** ramps from 0 on a clip with none.

**Normalize** sets the clip's own level whatever is selected, and its row shows a small "clip" tag while an action is selected.

See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).

## Text

An action can animate the **Text** sub-tab's style, size and colours.

| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content | | The words |
| Font | **Size** | **Family**, **Style** |
| Style | **Color**, **Line spacing**, **Tracking** | **Align**, **Vertical**, **UPPERCASE** |
| Outline | **Width**, **Color** | **Outline** |
| Backdrop | **Fill**, **Padding**, **Radius** | **Backdrop** |
| Box | **Width** | **Mode** |
| Reveal | **In**, **Out** | **Reveal** |

Choosing one of the **Presets** with an action selected sets the action's end state, and each value then ramps or switches as above.

A word caption page's timing can't animate, because it belongs to the speech. There's no inspector section for its word colours and pop scale, so only an agent can put those in an action. They ramp when it does. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).

For the rows themselves, see [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).

## Graphics

An action can animate a graphic clip's properties in the **Properties** section of the **Graphic** sub-tab. Numbers and colours ramp, while strings, booleans, choices and images switch at the end. A property the graphic marks as not animatable shows ⊘, and so do the **Size** and **Timeline** sections.

See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

## Speed

An action can change a media clip's playback rate, which makes a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/). With an action selected, **Rate** in the **Clip** sub-tab's **Speed** section sets the rate the action ends at, and the clip holds that rate afterwards.

- The rate goes from ×0.1 to ×1000.
- The clip keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source.
- Frame Job won't set a rate that would read past the end of the media, and it names the largest rate that fits.
- Above ×12 the clip's sound is left out, and Frame Job asks first. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** always change the clip.

## What never animates

These rows change the clip itself whatever is selected. They're marked ⊘ in the Clip tab while an action is selected, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."

- **Clip sub-tab:** the [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Keep pitch** and **Fit to** in the Speed section.
- **Sound sub-tab:** Ducking, the fade shapes (**In shape** and **Out shape**), the Voice Effect, and a nest clip's **Mix to mono**.
- **Picture sub-tab:** the [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) section, **Remove background** and **Subject** in the Background section, and **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle** in the Cursor section.
- **Filters and Obscure:** adding or removing a filter or a region. Changing a value inside an existing entry still animates.
- **Shape sub-tab:** a [shape's](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) kind, stroke, fill, gradient and arrows. Its position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's, through the **Picture** sub-tab. Dragging a shape's handles on the canvas to resize it changes the shape itself.
- **Graphic sub-tab:** the **Size** and **Timeline** sections, and any property the graphic marks as not animatable.

A track's own volume, pan, compressor and limiter aren't part of a clip, so an action can't reach them.

## Colours blend in OKLab

Every colour an action animates blends through the OKLab colour space. It keeps the midpoints even and avoids the muddy middle of a straight RGB blend. Pure red to pure blue passes through `#8c53a2` halfway, for example, where a straight RGB blend would give a dark purple.

This covers the shadow, chroma key, text, outline, backdrop, word caption and graphic colours. Opacity moves separately from the colour. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact all the way through, and there's no setting for any of this.

Shape colours can't animate at all.

- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)
